subject: Enclave activation and comms playbook
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops-team@newleaf.health>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enclave activation & security handoff — next steps

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again — NewLeaf is ready to move from onboarding discovery to enclave activation. We finished the baseline inventory and want to align on the immediate network/security prerequisites so the activation window doesn't hit surprises. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm required VPC/peering model (shared VPC vs. VPC peering) and whether cross-project routes will be used.
- Target egress flow (NAT vs. proxy) and any IP allowlist footprints we should prepare.
- KMS / HSM ownership: who will hold keys, expected CSR flow for import (if any).
- Any SOC2 addendum / logging requirements we should include in the go-live checklist.

I've attached our inventory export (newleaf-inventory-20270610.csv) with CIDRs and responsible folks. Can you share Redwood's preflight checklist and confirm a contact for the network handoff call? Ideally we'd run a short tech-sync next week.

Appreciate it,

Maya Chen
Director, Infrastructure — NewLeaf Health
maya.chen@newleaf.health

Attachments: newleaf-inventory-20270610.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops-team@newleaf.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enclave activation & security handoff — next steps

Hi Maya / NewLeaf ops team,

Thanks — appreciate the inventory. Attaching our Redwood on‑prem prereqs and a lightweight activation checklist (redwood-onprem-prereqs.pdf). High level responses to your asks:

- Recommended routing model: we support either shared VPC (recommended for GCP customers who want centralized control) or VPC peering with route advertisement. Shared VPC simplifies service account scoping.
- Egress: NAT is the most straightforward for predictable IPs; we also support an outbound proxy if you need application-level filtering. We'll provide the IP range for allowlisting once you pick the model.
- KMS: customers may retain key control (bring-your-own KMS) or use Redwood-managed envelope keys. If you want BYOK, we will provide an import guide and can coordinate HSM-backed key transfer.
- Logging: we require audit log forwarding (S3/GCS) and a minimum 90‑day retention for tracing relevant to quality/regression analysis. SOC2 addendum typically includes those fields — Marissa will follow up with the legal/Docusign flow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech handoff call — 60 minutes — pick a slot Mon/Tue next week.
2) You share CIDR blocks and peering preference; we'll produce a one‑page network diagram.
3) We exchange service account roles and KMS ownership model.

I'm looping in Dev for the technical specifics (ports, peering details, KMS notes).

Best,

Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-onprem-prereqs.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops-team@newleaf.health>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enclave activation & security handoff — technical details

Hi Maya / team,

Quick technical note to get the network/security engineering work queued. I'm listing the items we'll need and typical config values so your infra team can validate against the inventory:

Network & routing
- Allowed outbound IPs: Redwood will provide a /28 per environment for allowlisting (can be NAT IPs or proxy egress).
- Ports: 443 outbound to our endpoints; 22 only for approved jump hosts during provisioning windows (no permanent SSH).
- MTU: 1460 recommended for GCP interconnect; set jumbo frames only if you validate L3 path.
- BGP / route advertisement: if using dedicated interconnect, we'll exchange ASN and prefixes; otherwise static routes/peering fine.

Service accounts & IAM
- Principle of least privilege: create one service account per environment with roles: logging.write, monitoring.metricWriter, storage.objectViewer. We'll provide a JSON policy template.
- For cross-project access (shared VPC), grant service account token creator to the owning project if needed.

KMS / keys
- BYOK path: we support both raw key import and envelope-wrapping. If you want HSM-backed keys, follow the attached kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf. Please confirm: will NewLeaf hold master keys or have Redwood manage envelope keys?

Observability & retention
- Audit logs: forward to customer-managed bucket (s3://newleaf-redwood-logs) with UTF-8 gzip rotation; we consume via the shared ingestion pipeline.
- Traces: 90 days retention is required for regression alerts.

Drive link with config templates: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/Onprem-Onboarding-NewLeaf (has service-account-template.json, firewall-template.csv).

If NewLeaf can provide the CIDR list and confirm KMS ownership by EOD Monday we can finalize the network diagram and schedule the provisioning window.

Thanks,

Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf (PDF, 22KB)
